review.summary:
Lens: operability and release, round 3, on 8e76c63. HEAD is 394b261, which changes only crates/xtask/src/main.rs, .claude/carry.md and a skill since 8e76c63 (git diff --stat).

Fix checks, all verified by running or reading:
- ops-2 (R1, material): HOLDS. I ran the resolver's `build` from a copy of plugin/ with a temp PLANROOM_DATA and shim git, cargo and pnpm. The call order was `git clone --depth 1 --branch main`, then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`, then `cargo xtask gen --canvas`, then `cargo build --release --locked -p planroom`. The engine was then cached with `.ok` and `last_used`, the clone was removed, and `status --json` reported step `cache`.
- ops-3 (R1, material): HOLDS. README.md:8-9 and plugin/README.md give `/plugin marketplace add doodla/planroom` then `/plugin install planroom@planroom`. No shipped doc uses `--marketplace`.
- R2 material findings in this lens: none. The ops lens's round-2 findings were all minor.
- The resolver half of GUARD2's security-r2-1 fix (DR-86, "the resolver checks its cache"): HOLDS. I swapped the cached binary for a script, and `status --json` no longer resolved from the cache. `installer (ubuntu-24.04)` and `installer (macos-15)` are green in run 40355961410, including a_swapped_cached_engine_is_refused.
- drift-2's contract.sh (R1 spot check): HOLDS. The resolver sources it and spells no code itself.
- The plugin.json stamp `0.1.0-dev.gc3281fc5` matches my recomputation of plugin_hash.
- serve: `serve --detach` gives PGID = SID = pid with PPID 1. serve.json and the login page are 0600. After `kill -9`, a second `serve --detach` reuses the recorded port.
- A store bumped to user_version 2: watch prints one schema_mismatch envelope and exits 7. serve logs "the live loop stopped" and exits. serve.json is left behind, as round 2 found (ops-r2-10, still minor).

Still known gaps, no worse:
- ops-7: no release.yml, CHANGELOG, `gen --version`, check-tag-version.sh, SECURITY.md or dependabot.yml; release-dry-run has `if: false`; the package.json files say 0.1.0 while Cargo says 0.1.0-dev. A release still can't be cut from this tree, and the path-dependency pins (`=0.1.0-dev`) have nothing to rewrite them.
- ops-1 and security-7: the cache key is `$data/engine/$version`, while architecture.md states VERSION+HASH as if built.
- ops-r2-1: the README line reads main's `./plugin` entry, and the layout check requires exactly that, so no published git-subdir entry can exist.
- Also unchanged: ops-r2-2, -3, -4, -5, -7 and -8, ops-11 (data root created at 0755), and the empty serve.log (drift-11).

New and most important: CI has been red on every completed run since round 2's merges. macOS fails SCAN2's new test on every run, most likely from a non-physical temp path in the test. The Ubuntu job fails a different test each run. xtask's 80-line tail hides the assertion text, so CI logs can't show why.

On a clean machine, a first user installing from the marketplace still gets the dev-version source build. Its preflight can still promise "about 4 minutes" on toolchains that will fail.

What I assumed rather than verified:
- The exact macOS assertion that fails. The CI log doesn't print it; I reproduced the engine's physical-path output on Linux through a symlink.
- The cause of the Ubuntu budgets failure. It doesn't reproduce on Linux here, with or without the Ruby pack.
- Platform facts about Homebrew and Debian cargo versions, and Node or pnpm minimums.

findings.title: CI is red on every completed run since round 2's merges: macOS fails SCAN2's new test every time, and Ubuntu fails a different test each run
where: docs/contributing/decisions.md (DR-86 Sources: 'the merged tree's cargo xtask check, test, ...')
findings.evidence:
VERIFIED (read-only gh calls).

`gh run list --branch ccr-b124f0e3-xnzjca`: every completed run since the round-2 merge a5620e9 is `failure` (40349180778 on a5620e9, 40350501570 on 129f86c, 40355961410 on 394b261). Every other run since then was `cancelled`, including 8e76c63's (40355613412), so the reviewed commit never got a finished run. 394b261 differs from 8e76c63 only in xtask/main.rs, carry.md and a skill (`git diff --stat`).

`gh run view --log-failed`:
- test (macos-15) fails `planroom::scan an_unborn_and_an_unreadable_repo_leave_the_rest_of_the_workspace_mapped` in all three runs.
- test (ubuntu-24.04) fails `FAIL + LEAK planroom::live watch_frames_every_commit_of_three_writers_and_a_rescan_within_1_s` in 40350501570 and `planroom::budgets every_built_leafs_reply_on_the_fixture_keeps_to_its_budget` in 40355961410.

The macOS cause is LIKELY a test bug:
- `fixture()` returns `out.to_path_buf()` without canonicalizing (testkit/src/lib.rs:43).
- scan.rs:509 asserts `fix.contains("git -C {root}/broken status")`.
- The engine reports physical paths. I scanned a workspace through a symlinked path (link/ws -> real/ws) holding a broken repo, and the fix read `Run git -C .../real/ws/broken status ...`.
- macOS tempdirs are /var/folders/..., a link to /private/var/..., and DR-83 says the harnesses must take physical paths.

The Ubuntu budgets failure doesn't reproduce here. On a fixture I built with examples/build-fixture, with and without the Ruby pack config, every leaf stayed within budget (largest: schema --command focus at 1431/1500).
findings.why: KICKOFF S14 (tier A) requires 'CI is green on the pushed branch', and AGENTS.md requires `cargo xtask test` to pass before claiming success. DR-86 records that the merged tree's `cargo xtask test` passed, which holds only for the local Linux-as-root run, not macOS CI. While the job is red, a real regression on macOS (a supported platform) would be indistinguishable from this test bug. Two Ubuntu tests fail intermittently, one of them the 1 s live gate.
findings.fix: Canonicalize the fixture root in the test (or in `fixture()`), e.g. `let root = fixture(&dir.path().canonicalize().unwrap()).root;`. Rerun the Ubuntu job with full failure output (see ops-r3-2) to fix or deflake the budgets and live-watch tests. Don't let a merge's CI run be cancelled by the carry-note push that follows it.

findings.title: xtask keeps only the last 80 lines of a failed step, so CI logs never show why a Rust test failed
findings.evidence:
VERIFIED.
- `Report::failed` prints `lines[len-80..]` of the step's captured output (report.rs:139-141).
- nextest prints a failing test's stdout and stderr when the test finishes (`--failure-output` defaults to immediate), mid-run, so the tail holds only PASS lines and the summary.
- The full job logs I saved: the macOS job (121688935311) and the Ubuntu job (121688935514) of run 40355961410 contain no `panicked`, `assertion`, `left:` or `STDERR` line. Only the `---- cargo nextest run ----` header and the FAIL line survive.
findings.why: The red CI in ops-r3-1 can't be diagnosed from CI at all, which is why its cause here is an inference. Platform-only failures (macOS paths, timing on runners) are exactly what local runs can't show.
findings.fix: For test steps, pass `--failure-output final` (or `immediate-final`) to nextest and print the step's whole output on failure, or at least everything from the first FAIL block. Alternatively, upload the full output as a job artifact.

findings.title: The source-build preflight checks the Rust version only in a checkout, and Node and pnpm only for presence, so the first user's card promises a 4-minute build that fails
where: docs/contributing/architecture.md (The source build: 'cargo at or above the workspace's rust-version')
findings.evidence:
VERIFIED by running. I ran a copy of plugin/ outside any checkout (the marketplace-install case) with `env -i PATH=<dir>`: a `cargo` that prints `cargo 1.75.0`, no rustup, and cc, git, node and pnpm linked in. `scripts/planroom version --json` answered `engine_unavailable`, reason `no_release`, 'Build it from source, about 4 minutes', `est_minutes: 4`, `canvas: true`.

The rust-version comparison sits inside `if ! command -v rustup ... && checkout=$(checkout_dir)` (:332). Outside a checkout there's no Cargo.toml to read, so it never runs. The clone's Cargo.toml says `rust-version = "1.97"`.

`canvas=true` is set whenever `node` and `pnpm` are on PATH (:351-354). No version is checked, though the workspace pins Node 22.22.0 (.node-version) and pnpm 10.28.2 with a v9 lockfile.

ASSUMED from platform knowledge: distro and older Homebrew cargo builds are below 1.97, and an older Node or pnpm fails `vite build` or `--frozen-lockfile`.
findings.why: On the only install path that exists until a release (a -dev plugin, so the clone build), the person accepts a card that says it will work. The build then fails after cloning and partly compiling. It's a known class (ops-r2-7), but this gap isn't listed there, and it contradicts architecture.md's preflight, whose job is 'never a card for a build that will fail'.
findings.fix: Write the workspace's rust-version into engine.env with `gen` and compare against it whether or not there's a checkout. When rustup is absent, require that version; when it's present, the toolchain file decides. Check `node --version` against the major version in .node-version, and the pnpm major, before reporting `canvas: true`.

findings.title: A failed source build leaves its clone and partial target directory under the data root until the next build
findings.evidence:
VERIFIED with shims (a fake cargo that exits 101 on `build --release`). `scripts/planroom build` printed `error: boom` and exited 101. `ls data/src` still held `0.1.0-dev/`.

The script runs under `set -e`, so a failed `git clone`, canvas step or `cargo build` exits at once. The only `rm -rf "$src"` is after a successful install (:419) or at the start of the next build (:402). No trap removes it, and the mod's failure line (register.tsx:239-249) names none of this.
findings.why: A release build's target directory runs to gigabytes, as the resolver's own comment says (:418). After a failed build, or the mod's 600 s timeout killing one, that disk stays used under ~/.local/share/planroom/src/ with nothing telling the person. It's freed only if they press Build again.
findings.fix: Set a trap in build() that removes `$src` on any non-zero exit, as take_lock does for `$tmp`. Or keep the clone only for a retry the person starts, and say where it is in the failure line.

findings.title: `version --json` never reports git_commit, so nothing identifies which main commit a -dev engine was built from
findings.evidence:
VERIFIED.
- `target/debug/planroom version --json` reports `"version":"0.1.0-dev","git_commit":null`.
- version.rs:27 reads `option_env!("PLANROOM_GIT_COMMIT")`, but build.rs sets only `PLANROOM_TARGET` (`grep -rn PLANROOM_GIT_COMMIT crates/` finds only that read).
- contracts.md:344 and DR-82 document `git_commit` in VersionInfo.
- Every -dev engine reports the same version, and the resolver caches it under `engine/0.1.0-dev` with no hash (ops-1).
findings.why: Until a release, every user's engine is a clone build of some main commit (the resolver clones `--branch main`). With no commit in VersionInfo, and a version-only cache key, neither the person nor a bug report (doctor, M5) can tell which code is running after a plugin update. That makes ops-1's stale-engine problem undiagnosable.
findings.fix: In build.rs, set `PLANROOM_GIT_COMMIT` from `git rev-parse HEAD` when the build runs in a git checkout (with rerun-if-changed on .git/HEAD), and leave it null otherwise.

findings.title: A rebuild swaps the cached binary before rewriting its .ok stamp, so a resolve in that window treats the cache as missing
findings.evidence:
VERIFIED by reading.
- build() runs `cp built planroom.new`, then `mv -f planroom.new planroom`, then `sha256_of planroom > .ok`, then touch_last_used (:413-417). The old `.ok` stays in place until the redirect truncates and rewrites it.
- download() instead removes `.ok` first and writes `.ok.new` and renames it (:310-312).
- cache_ok (round 2's GUARD2 fix) requires `.ok` to be non-empty and to match the binary's sha256.
- Between the mv and the end of the hash write (a hash of a tens-of-MB binary), a concurrent resolve finds a mismatch. For a -dev version that falls through to `offer_build` with `engine_unavailable`/`no_release` (:480-481), so a skill's Bash call or a reloading mod is told to build again mid-rebuild.
findings.why: This is a narrow race the round-2 cache check introduced on the build path. It can't run a wrong binary, but it can send a second session into a second build, which deletes the first build's clone (ux-k).
findings.fix: Write the stamp the way download() does: `rm -f .ok`, hash `planroom.new` into `.ok.new`, `mv planroom.new planroom`, then `mv .ok.new .ok`. Also take the fetch lock around build()'s install step.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed with read-only gh calls. `gh run list` shows every completed run since round 2's merge failed: 40349180778, 40350501570 and 40355961410. Every other run in that period, including 8e76c63's 40355613412, was cancelled, and the last success is 40343743319, from before the merges. `gh run view --log-failed` shows test (macos-15) failing `planroom::scan an_unborn_and_an_unreadable_repo_leave_the_rest_of_the_workspace_mapped` in all three runs. Ubuntu failed `live watch_frames_every_commit_of_three_writers_and_a_rescan_within_1_s` (FAIL + LEAK) in 40350501570 and `budgets every_built_leafs_reply_on_the_fixture_keeps_to_its_budget` in 40355961410. The test compares against a path that isn't canonicalized: scan.rs:474 calls `fixture(dir.path()).root`, testkit/src/lib.rs:43 returns `out.to_path_buf()`, and scan.rs:509 builds `git -C {root}/broken status`. decisions.md:2013 itself notes that macOS reports /private/var for /var temp paths. So the reviewer's likely cause is plausible, but it is an inference: the CI log holds no assertion text. KICKOFF.md:127 puts S14 in tier A, and :189 requires 'CI is green on the pushed branch'. The review README doesn't log this as a known gap. Material holds.

Confirmed. report.rs:136-145 prints only the last 80 lines of a failed step. main.rs:490-494 runs `nextest run --no-fail-fast` without `--failure-output`, and there is no `.config/nextest.toml`. Grepping run 40355961410's failed log for panicked, assertion, left:, STDERR or STDOUT finds 0 matches. The tail shows only PASS lines and the summary. This is a diagnosability gap, not a scenario failure, so minor is right.

Confirmed by reading plugin/scripts/planroom:325-356. The rust-version check sits inside `if ! command -v rustup ... && checkout=$(checkout_dir)`, so it never runs outside a checkout. `canvas=true` rests only on `command -v node` and `pnpm`, with no version checked. I didn't rerun the reviewer's shim test. ops-r2-7, a logged known gap, covers missing git, the macOS xcode shims and PATH after rustup, but not an old cargo outside a checkout or old Node and pnpm versions, so this is a distinct gap. It is the same class of preflight miss, and a failed build is visible and recoverable, so minor.

Confirmed by reading. The script runs under `set -eu` (:15). build() at :402-419 removes `$src` only before cloning and after a successful install. Its only traps are take_lock's (:212), which don't cover build(). The exit at :412, taken when main is newer than the plugin, also leaves the clone behind. The disk is reclaimed on the next build of the same version, so this is a disk-use problem, not data loss. Minor.

Confirmed. `target/debug/planroom version --json` returns `"git_commit":null`. version.rs:27 reads `option_env!("PLANROOM_GIT_COMMIT")`, and grep finds nothing in crates/, plugin/ or .github/ that sets it, release.yml included. contract command.rs:593 types the field as Option, so null is a valid value, but no build path ever fills it. It's a diagnosability gap, so minor.

Confirmed by reading. build() at :413-417 runs `mv planroom.new planroom` and only then `sha256_of > .ok`. The redirect truncates `.ok` first, so `-s` fails, and until it is rewritten the old hash mismatches. cache_ok at :152-156 then fails, and a -dev resolve falls to offer_build (:480-481). download() at :310-312 uses the rm, .ok.new and mv order instead. The race only matters when a rebuild runs while the cache is valid, since resolve offers a build only when cache_ok fails. That rebuild is a documented path: architecture.md:1298 says 'Install Node 22 and pnpm, then run scripts/planroom build' for a canvas-less engine. The window lasts only as long as one hash, and it can't run a wrong binary. Minor.
